$comment: Single source of truth for the package versions every adopting repository
is held to. It names VERSIONS and never repositories: this repo has no
list of who consumes it, and should not -- a repository opts in by calling
job-ci-conformance, and the checker is handed one clone at a time.
Nothing reads this at build time — each repo still declares its own pin in
the file its tooling actually reads (package.json packageManager,
package.json devDependencies, go.mod, .node-version), because that is what
pnpm/action-setup, pnpm, setup-go and setup-node consume in CI, and what
the npm install of standards/016-local-development.md LD6 reads on a
developer's machine and in an image. This file is what those per-repo
pins are checked AGAINST: tools/check-dependency-versions compares every
repo to the values here, so drift is a failing check rather than
something noticed months later. Bumping a version here is the start of a
wave, not the end: update the value, then update every repo's own pin to
$packageManager_comment: reads it in the shared jobs; the npm install of LD6 reads it on a
developer's machine and in an image (standards/016-local-development.md).
